title: PBH 201 - Principles of Public Health
topics: Concept and scope of public health
Health systems and their building blocks

items.q: The statement “measures taken before disease begins that stop it occurring at all” describes which of the following?
o: Primary prevention
Health protection
Primordial prevention
Prevention paradox
items.s: Primary prevention is measures taken before disease begins that stop it occurring at all.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Selective primary health care.
o: a narrow set of cheap technical fixes aimed at the commonest causes of death
care that limits disability and helps a person with established disease to function
the core task of using evidence to decide priorities and design responses
the organisation of staff, supplies and facilities into care that reaches those in need
items.s: Selective primary health care: a narrow set of cheap technical fixes aimed at the commonest causes of death. The other options describe Policy development, Tertiary prevention, Service delivery.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Social marketing?
o: the agreed route by which a patient moves between levels of care
the use of commercial selling techniques to make a beneficial behaviour attractive
the delivery of vaccines that make a person resistant to a specific infection
the degree to which records are complete, consistent and free of error
items.s: Social marketing: the use of commercial selling techniques to make a beneficial behaviour attractive. The other options describe Data quality, Referral system, Immunisation.

items.q: Which term is described by “money handed over directly by a patient at the point of receiving care”?
o: Health system
Health financing
Universal health coverage
Out-of-pocket payment
items.s: Out-of-pocket payment is money handed over directly by a patient at the point of receiving care.
items.t: Health systems and their building blocks

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Genetic endowment.
o: care that limits disability and helps a person with established disease to function
the basic set of services a district promises to make available to everyone
the physician who showed that handwashing by delivery attendants cut fatal childbed fever
the inherited make-up that sets a person's baseline susceptibility to illness
items.s: Genetic endowment: the inherited make-up that sets a person's baseline susceptibility to illness. The other options describe Tertiary prevention, Essential package, Ignaz Semmelweis.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Ottawa Charter.
o: the air, soil, housing and workplace conditions surrounding people
the 1986 statement naming healthy public policy and supportive settings as key actions
a structured interview with relatives used to assign a cause after a death at home
the principle that services are shared according to need rather than ability to pay
items.s: Ottawa Charter: the 1986 statement naming healthy public policy and supportive settings as key actions. The other options describe Verbal autopsy, Equitable distribution, Physical environment.

items.q: The statement “measures such as clean water, safe food and pest control that reduce exposure to hazards” describes which of the following?

Primary prevention
Health protection
Immunisation
items.s: Health protection is measures such as clean water, safe food and pest control that reduce exposure to hazards.

items.q: All of the following belong to Health promotion and education EXCEPT
o: Ottawa Charter
Health promotion
Healthy public policy
Ratio
items.s: Every other option belongs to Health promotion and education. “Ratio” belongs to Measuring the health of populations, not Health promotion and education.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Data quality?

the degree to which records are complete, consistent and free of error
the duty to keep personal records private except with consent or legal need
measures such as clean water, safe food and pest control that reduce exposure to hazards
items.s: Data quality: the degree to which records are complete, consistent and free of error. The other options describe Health protection, Confidentiality, High-risk approach.

items.q: Primordial prevention may be defined as
o: action that stops the emergence of risk factors in a population in the first place
the routine registers and reports through which services track the people they serve
the core task of making sure agreed services are actually delivered and of good quality
the agreed route by which a patient moves between levels of care
items.s: Primordial prevention: action that stops the emergence of risk factors in a population in the first place. The other options describe Assurance, Health information system, Referral system.

Public health

Population approach
items.s: Community diagnosis is the systematic study of the problems and resources of a defined locality.

the global goal of making essential services available to every person in every country
